explanation: Ownership of land or property is not a mode of acquiring citizenship. The modes are birth, descent, registration, naturalisation and incorporation of territory.

q: To acquire citizenship in India, at least how long must an applicant have stayed in the country?
explanation:
the 5-year rule was changed by the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2003 (in force 3 Dec 2004) — now naturalisation needs 12 years (11 of 14 + 12 months), registration of a PIO 7 years, CAA communities 5 years (Citizenship Act Third Schedule)
In 2003 naturalisation needed one year's residence plus four of the preceding seven years, i.e. 5 years in all, the exam key (now 12 years for naturalisation and 7 for registration of a PIO).

q: Which of the following is NOT a criterion for acquiring citizenship of India, subject to other conditions?
explanation: Citizenship is acquired by birth, descent, registration, naturalisation or incorporation of territory; ethnic identity is not a criterion.

notes.text: - **Arts. 5–8** are the Articles that define the categories of citizens at commencement (APPSC G2 Mains 2017 key "Articles 5 to 8"); Arts. 9–11 are general provisions.

q: What is minimum duration of stay essential before a person can apply for citizenship in India?
explanation:
the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2003 raised the residence for registration from 5 to 7 years — now 7 years (registration) and 12 years (naturalisation; 5 years under the CAA, 2019) (Citizenship Act, 1955 as amended)
When asked (2003), citizenship by registration needed 5 years' ordinary residence in India. (now 7 years for registration; naturalisation needs 12 years – 11 in the preceding 14 plus the last 12 months – or 5 years for the communities covered by the CAA, 2019)

notes.text: - Citizen-only offices: **President, Vice-President, SC/HC judges, Governor, Attorney General, Advocate General**.

q: What is the minimum duration of stay essential before a person can apply for Indian citizenship?
explanation:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (12 years); it is added as option 5.
Printed key '10 years' matches no provision of the Citizenship Act; if the stem means registration, 7 years would be the answer.
For naturalisation a person must reside in India for the 12 months before applying and for 11 of the 14 years before that – 12 years in all (5 years for the CAA communities since 2019). 7 years applies only to registration of persons of Indian origin or spouses of citizens, and none of the printed periods is the naturalisation requirement.

key_text: Article 4 to 10 deal with the Rights of Citizenship of certain migrants to Pakistan, Indian Origin residing outside India
explanation: The wrong statement is C: migrants to Pakistan and persons of Indian origin abroad are Articles 7 and 8, and Part II is Articles 5-11, not 4-10. There is one domicile, and foreign citizenship voluntarily acquired ends Indian citizenship (Art. 9).

q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers the Parliament to regulate the rights of the citizens
explanation: Article 11 empowers Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law. Article 10 only continues citizenship subject to such law.
